svg.title: Where each kind of workload goes
svg.desc: An intermediate root management group sits at the top with three branches. Platform holds four groups: Security, Management, Connectivity and Identity, for shared services. Landing zones holds Corp for internal apps that need the hub network, Online for internet-facing apps, Local for workloads on Azure Local, and an optional extra group for a subset with an extra compliance rule. Sandboxes holds experiments, and Decommissioned holds cancelled subscriptions. A note says development, test and production are subscriptions in the same group, not groups. Own layout by the author, not an official Microsoft diagram.
svg.text: Where each kind of workload goes
The group a subscription sits in decides which policies it inherits.
Ask where the workload connects: the hub means Corp, the internet means Online, Azure Local means Local.
Add an extra group under Landing zones only for a subset of workloads with a real extra rule.
Development, test and production are subscriptions in the same group. They are not groups.
Platform subscriptions hold shared services. Workloads do not go there.
A new subscription goes where its policies should apply, not where its team sits on the org chart.
